what: A port sampler running on the modem's own 80186, hooked onto the tick, writing I/O port reads into a RAM ring buffer at 200 Hz.

idle_capture.note: identical to what the serial sweep reports at idle, which is the cross-check that the sampler reads what it claims to

the_finding.claim: AT&T8 clears essentially all free RAM.
the_finding.evidence: 51 marker bytes placed across every free region from 0x0e77 to 0x0fc77; after one AT&T8 / AT&T0 cycle, 0 of 51 survived. The control was unarmed - no routine was hooked and no code executed - so this is the firmware's own behaviour, not a crash.
the_finding.consequence: AT&T8 cannot be used as the stimulus for a RAM-resident sampler: it destroys the routine, the cursor and the buffer. It is also why the first armed attempt returned an empty buffer.

limits: The idle capture shows no movement, which is expected: the serial sweep already said these four ports are static on hook. It proves the instrument, not the ASIC.
Sampling 0x1c and 0x1e races the supervisor for mailbox status, which is tolerable for a short idle run and would not be for a live call.
200 Hz is the tick rate, not the codec rate; events shorter than 5 ms are still invisible.
